community.headline: Volunteers wanted for Tesco winter food collection on 26 to 28 November
community.summary: Volunteers are sought for three-hour shifts at collection points in large Tesco stores, supporting Trussell food banks and the Felix charity network.
points: Runs 26 to 28 November in all large Tesco stores
Shifts take about three hours
Last year's collection gave almost 1.5 million meals
body: Foodbanks and food charities are looking for volunteers to stand at collection points in large Tesco stores for the supermarket's Winter Food Collection, which runs from 26 to 28 November. Volunteering takes about three hours, and the charities say having people in store significantly increases how much food is given.

This is the 14th year of the collection, run with charity partners Trussell and Felix, and last year shoppers donated almost 1.5 million meals' worth of food. One in five Trussell food parcels comes from Tesco and its customers, and more than half of the charities in the Felix network, which spans over 8,000 local groups, report rising demand over the past year.

People can sign up through the Trussell or Felix websites to help at their nearest large Tesco. Trussell's co-chief executive Matthew van Duyvenbode said volunteers were urgently needed to play their part.

courts.headline: Eastwood dog owner to be sentenced in December after 15 German shepherds were rescued from his home
courts.summary: Terence Snooks was convicted of 15 animal welfare offences after a joint council and police raid, in what officers called one of the worst neglect cases they had seen in 30 years.
body: Terence Snooks, of Eastwood, was convicted at Basildon Magistrates’ Court on 1 September of 15 offences under section 9 of the Animal Welfare Act 2006, Southend-on-Sea City Council says. The case came after council and police officers removed 15 German shepherd dogs from a property in Eastwood in February 2025, following residents’ complaints about persistent barking and the state of the property.

The council says the dogs lacked proper food, fresh water, bedding, exercise and socialisation, and the house and garden were heavily contaminated with faeces and urine. Many of the animals had matted fur and overgrown claws, several were underweight, and three were so badly affected that they had to be put to sleep. Five went to a specialist breed rehabilitation centre and most of the rest have been rehomed.

ITV News reported the case on Wednesday. Snooks is due to be sentenced at Basildon Magistrates’ Court on 8 December. Councillor Irene Ferguson said the result showed the council would act on serious welfare concerns.
points: Raid on the Eastwood property took place in February 2025

official.headline: Rochford leader urges ministers to lift block on Local Plan and allow more time to consult
official.summary: A Government holding direction in place since 2 October stops the council starting its final round of public consultation.
body: Rochford District Council has called on the Government to decide quickly on its Local Plan and lift the holding direction that has paused it since 2 October. The council says it cannot start the final public consultation while the direction stays in place, and is also asking for the submission deadline to be extended, which it believes could run to March.

Council leader Cllr Adi Malviya said the district needs an up-to-date plan to avoid speculative applications in the wrong places. The council says it sent the evidence ministers requested on 7 October, and that before the direction it was on track to submit by the 31 December deadline.

If the direction is lifted without an extension, the council says consultation would probably run over Christmas and close on the day the plan must be submitted, leaving councillors no time to consider responses. Separately, the public inquiry into the Mount Bovers appeal on land west of Main Road, Hawkwell, resumes on 8 December.

body: Tendring District Council has granted Clacton Town Football Club Ltd a temporary licence to use the Rush Green Bowl on Rush Green Road, Clacton, for the rest of the 2026/27 season. The council says the licence formalises the club’s current occupation of the council-owned ground, with safeguards for the site, and keeps it open for football and community use.

The council says it has been working to resolve longstanding issues around the ground’s occupation. Councillor Peter Kotz, cabinet member for assets, said the licence keeps football going at the site and welcomed improvements the club has made to the ground.
Next, the council plans an open and fair tender for a longer-term lease. It says whoever wins the lease may be able to apply for Football Association funding.

Nomination papers must reach the Returning Officer, Colin Ansell, by 4pm on Friday 13 November. Residents who are not yet registered have until midnight on Tuesday 24 November to sign up, and postal vote applications close at 5pm on Wednesday 25 November.

official.headline: Last chance for Southend residents to comment on Local Plan the Government ordered the council to publish
official.summary: The Regulation 19 consultation on where homes, jobs and infrastructure could go across the city runs until Monday 21 December, before the plan goes to a planning inspector.
body: Southend-on-Sea City Council has opened the final round of public consultation on its draft Local Plan, the document that will guide where new homes, employment land, infrastructure and community facilities may go across the city. It runs from Friday 6 November until Monday 21 December 2026.

The council said central government formally directed it on 23 October to publish the draft for consultation by 6 November, and the cabinet agreed unanimously on 5 November to do so. Comments at this stage must address whether the plan is legally compliant and sound under national planning policy. Cllr Kevin Robinson, cabinet member for planning, property and governance, urged residents to read the draft and respond.

Documents and the response form are on the council's Local Plan website, with paper copies at Southend libraries and the Civic Centre reception. Full council is due to consider the final plan in early 2027, when it will be submitted for independent examination by a planning inspector.

body: An Essex Police officer has been dismissed after a misconduct panel found he behaved in a coercive and controlling way towards female colleagues. PC Ben Norfolk was found to have committed gross misconduct at a hearing chaired by Assistant Chief Constable Glen Pavelin.

The allegations considered at the hearing related to his behaviour towards three colleagues between 2024 and 2025, and included sending intimate images of himself in uniform and suggesting sexual activity at work. Mr Pavelin called the conduct completely unacceptable and said it showed a complete disregard for the oath the officer took.

body: Colchester City Council's grounds maintenance service transferred to Amphora, the company the council wholly owns, on 1 November. The service looks after parks, sports grounds, open spaces, housing land, cemeteries and the crematorium across the city.

Around 40 former Idverde employees moved across, and council and Amphora staff marked the change with volunteering days at Castle Park on 2 and 3 November, clearing leaves and planting hundreds of spring bulbs. The service covers almost 13,000 assets over more than 870 hectares. Cllr Martin Goss, portfolio holder for waste, neighbourhoods and leisure, welcomed the new colleagues into the council family.
The council says the arrangement gives it more flexibility to respond to local priorities and to find new ways of improving parks and green spaces, while keeping investment in the local area.

body: Essex Police's Rural Engagement Team has been awarded £57,721 from the Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner's Safer Streets fund to step up its fight against crime in the countryside. The money will be used across rural Essex, including the Dengie, where police have recently been cracking down on hare coursing.

The grant will buy a John Deere Gator all-terrain vehicle for remote locations, mobile number plate recognition cameras for three vehicles, trail cameras and signs for hotspots, and training for officers to drive the vehicle.

official.headline: Police appeal after three men claiming to be officers targeted people in Tilbury before dawn
official.summary: Police say a wallet and keys were taken in one of three incidents around St Chads Road and Calcutta Road early on Saturday 7 November.
body: Essex Police is appealing for witnesses after men claiming to be police officers approached people in Tilbury between 4am and 4.45am on Saturday 7 November. Police say the men were not in uniform and showed no identification, and nobody was hurt.

In one incident near the Tesco Express on Calcutta Road, two men got out of a white car and took a man's wallet and keys, police said. Officers say a taxi driver was also targeted on St Chads Road and another man was approached in the area. Police described three men, one in a high-visibility jacket and two in dark tracksuits, using a large white SUV-style car.

Grays CID is asking anyone who saw anything, or who was driving in the area with a dash cam, to come forward. Police say genuine officers will show their warrant card when asked and understand if people want to check their identity.

body: Gymnasts Emily and Abigail Roper have returned to the University of Essex, where they study Sports and Exercise Science at the Colchester campus, after making Commonwealth Games history for Wales, the university reports. The 21-year-old twins were back on campus in their Essex Blades kit, holding up their Team Wales shirts from Glasgow 2026.

Abigail won bronze on vault with a score of 13.433, Wales' first Commonwealth Games vault medal since 1994. Emily, who had just missed out on the vault podium in fourth, took bronze on the uneven bars less than an hour later.

The sisters joined Essex on a sports scholarship in autumn 2025 with Glasgow as their goal. They train at Pipers Vale Gymnastics Club in Ipswich and also compete for the Essex Blades in student competitions, where Emily won gold and Abigail bronze at the BUCS championships in February.

body: Essex batter Jordan Cox and seamer Sam Cook have both been named in England's 15-man Test squad to tour South Africa this winter, Essex Cricket has announced. Billy Munday headed the hosts in front inside two minutes from an Alfie Paxman corner, and Rowan Liburd made it two on 15 minutes after Aveley goalkeeper Jamie Grossart dropped the ball at his feet. Paxman added a third on 77 minutes and Latrell Lewis struck in the 90th, while Ramsgate keeper Jonny Henly also saved a penalty from Malachi Napa.

The defeat leaves Aveley fifteenth in the table. Their next game is away at Hutton in the Essex Senior Cup on Wednesday 11 November, and they return to league action at Carshalton on Saturday 21 November.

stories.headline: Southend mark 20 years since Eastwood sank Manchester United, as Sam Austin rejoins Kidderminster on loan
stories.summary: BBC Essex revisits the night Roots Hall beat Sir Alex Ferguson's side in the League Cup, while forward Sam Austin heads back to Aggborough for the rest of the season.
body: Saturday marks 20 years since Southend United beat Manchester United 1-0 at Roots Hall in the fourth round of the League Cup, on 7 November 2006. Freddy Eastwood's 27th-minute free-kick settled the tie in front of 11,532 fans, with Southend then bottom of the Championship, and BBC Essex has released a four-part podcast in which those involved relive the win.

Sir Alex Ferguson made nine changes but still fielded ten internationals, including Wayne Rooney and Cristiano Ronaldo, who was twice denied by goalkeeper Darryl Flahavan. Then manager Steve Tilson recalled that the players feared the worst when they saw the teamsheet. Southend went on to take Tottenham to extra time in the quarter-final before losing to a Jermain Defoe goal.

In current squad news, the club confirmed on Thursday that Sam Austin has joined Kidderminster Harriers on loan, and Kidderminster say the move runs until the end of the season. Austin, who left Aggborough four years ago for Notts County, told the Harriers he had always kept a place in his heart for the club and felt the timing was right.

stories.headline: No direct summer flight from Stansted to Florence once British Airways leaves the airport
stories.summary: British Airways CityFlyer is pulling out of the Uttlesford airport after the 2026/27 ski season, but Ryanair will keep flying to Bergerac, Nice, Olbia and Palma.
body: The last scheduled British Airways flights from Stansted leave on Sunday 11 April 2027, Chelmsford City Hub reports. The airline's summer timetable for next year drops all five of its warm-weather routes from the airport: Bergerac, Nice, Florence, Olbia in Sardinia and Palma de Mallorca.

Nice had been flown daily, Palma three times a day and Olbia twice a week, according to Simple Flying. Most of that demand will not be stranded: Ryanair plans to keep flying from Stansted to Bergerac, Nice, Olbia and Palma next summer, and Jet2 and TUI serve some of the same airports.

British Airways said it regularly reviews its network against demand and will use the aircraft elsewhere. It has not said whether the routes were losing money. CityFlyer first flew from Stansted in 2016, stopped during the Covid-19 pandemic and came back in 2024; its main base remains London City Airport.

stories.headline: Colchester council says it delivered 100 affordable homes between April and September
stories.summary: Colchester City Council's half-year performance report also counts 616 households in temporary accommodation and progress on Trinity Square and St Botolph's Circus.
body: The figure covers April to September 2026 and comes from a half-year performance report that went to Colchester City Council's Scrutiny Panel on Wednesday 11 November. Council leader Paul Dundas called it a positive step at a time of extremely high demand for housing.

Of the 100 homes, 37 came through partnerships with registered providers, 13 through the council's own building and buying programme and 50 through Section 106 agreements with developers. The report says 3,311 households got cost-of-living help in the six months, and five play parks were improved.

The report goes to Colchester City Council's Cabinet on Wednesday 2 December 2026. It says work on Trinity Square is expected to finish in early 2027, building is under way at St Botolph's Circus and on the East Hill cycle route, and residents are being consulted on a new bus station interchange and the new Local Plan.

stories.summary: Hanningfield and Abberton, which supply much of mid and south Essex, held 37% of their capacity on 10 November, below average for the time of year, Essex & Suffolk Water says.
body: In June, the company's total supply stood at 83%, the BBC reports. Katie Davies, Essex & Suffolk Water's head of water service planning, told the BBC the November level was "below where we'd expect to be at this time of year".
Essex & Suffolk Water brought in a Temporary Use Ban, or hosepipe ban, at 00:01 on Monday 3 August 2026 after a long hot and dry spell. It says the ban remains in force across its supply area.

The BBC reports that the Environment Agency still lists the East of England as in drought and names Hanningfield among eight reservoirs or reservoir groups in England with exceptionally low levels. The company says its advice to conserve water will stay in place until a considerable amount of rain has fallen.

stories.headline: Senior doctors' walkout that threatened Harlow hospital appointments is paused for pay talks
stories.summary: Consultants at Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow and across England will no longer strike later this month after the British Medical Association paused action to negotiate with the government.
body: Patients at Princess Alexandra Hospital had been warned to expect disruption to appointments and planned operations from 6.59am on Wednesday 25 November, when consultants were due to walk out for two days and provide emergency cover only. The hospital had asked people to keep their appointments unless contacted, Your Harlow reported.

The BMA's consultants committee, led by co-chairs Dr Helen Neary and Dr Shanu Datta, called off the action on 11 November to open talks with the government, NewsWire Explorer reports. Consultants received a 3.5% rise this year; the union wants the standard week cut from 40 to 35 hours, better pay for out-of-hours work and changes to pensions.

Health Secretary Yvette Cooper called it welcome news for patients and the wider NHS. Formal negotiations could begin in the week of 12 November, though ministers say a bigger pay rise this year is not on offer. In the strike ballot, 76% of consultants who voted backed action, on a turnout of just over half.

stories.headline: Suspected drug-drivers in Essex barred from driving for up to six weeks while police investigate
stories.summary: Essex Police says it is one of the first forces in the country to use bail conditions this way, as drug-driving arrests across the county keep rising.
body: Essex Police is using bail conditions to stop people suspected of drug-driving from driving while its inquiries continue, the BBC reported on Thursday 12 November 2026. Adam Pipe, head of the force's roads policing unit, said the aim was to speed up justice, because court backlogs and delays in testing blood samples can leave suspects driving for months before any disqualification.

Your Harlow reports that the policy, introduced in July, lets a custody sergeant attach a condition not to drive to pre-charge bail when a suspect cannot be charged straight away, for example while blood or urine results are still awaited. The suspect can make representations before the custody sergeant decides.

Essex Police says the condition may be used after collisions causing serious injury, after dangerous driving following a police pursuit, or when a driver is already awaiting prosecution for another drink or drug driving offence. Mr Pipe described it as an interim driving restriction before a case reaches court.

stories.summary: Keith Silk was given two years and 11 months at Chelmsford Crown Court for violent disorder and criminal damage outside the hotel.
body: The Torrington Drive, Loughton, man had been found guilty after a trial on 1 June, Your Harlow and the BBC report. The disorder outside the Bell Hotel in Epping took place on 17 July 2025, and he was sentenced on Tuesday 10 November.

The BBC reports that Silk threw a beer bottle at a police van and tried to pull a hotel sign out of the ground, and prosecutor Harriet Palfreman said he threatened officers. His barrister said he had been experiencing sensory overload, but Judge Alexander Mills said Silk chose to stay and placed himself at the heart of events.

Essex Police figures reported by Your Harlow put immediate custody over the protest at more than 23 years, while 11 others have received community orders, fines or suspended sentences. Chief Inspector Terry Fisher said the disorder left the community scared and anxious.
points: Silk was convicted after a trial on 1 June
The protest outside the hotel was on 17 July 2025
11 others have had community orders, fines or suspended sentences

stories.headline: Police ask for dash cam footage after man in his 80s dies following Mount Bures crash on Hall Road
stories.summary: A woman in her 70s is still being treated in hospital after a car struck both pedestrians on Sunday afternoon.
body: The pair were hit on Hall Road in Mount Bures at about 1pm on Sunday 8 November, the BBC reports, and the man died the following day.
Essex Police said no arrests had been made and asked anyone with information, CCTV or dash cam footage to come forward.
points: The man died on Monday, a day after the collision
No arrests have been made, police told the BBC

stories.headline: National Highways asks Thurrock to hold off on 200-home Grey Goose Farm scheme in Grays until February as residents object
stories.summary: Persimmon wants outline permission for homes north of Long Lane, but the roads agency says more modelling is needed on the busy North Stifford junction first.
body: Persimmon Homes Essex has asked Thurrock Council for outline permission to build up to 200 homes at Grey Goose Farm, north of Long Lane in Grays, half of them shared ownership or below-market rent. Sixteen of the 17 public comments lodged so far object, citing traffic, stretched GP and dental services and lost countryside.
National Highways wants no approval before 3 February 2027 while it models the A13/A1012 North Stifford junction. Persimmon says the site is a logical extension of the town.
points: Up to 200 homes, half shared ownership or below-market rent
16 of 17 public comments are objections
National Highways wants no approval before 3 February 2027

stories.headline: Hidden faces, street drinking and e-scooters on footpaths could all bring fines in Harlow under council plans open until 5 January
stories.summary: Harlow Council wants residents' views on a package of Public Space Protection Orders, some town-wide and some for set places, with breaches punishable by fixed penalties or prosecution.
body: Harlow Council has opened a consultation on a wide package of Public Space Protection Orders aimed at antisocial behaviour, intimidation and nuisance, Your Harlow reports. Options include banning face coverings used to hide identity during antisocial behaviour, e-scooters and cycling in pedestrian areas, street drinking, public drug use and aggressive begging.

Some measures could apply across the town and others only in set places. Breaches could bring fixed penalty notices or prosecution, and council leader Dan Swords said Harlow would not be a soft touch. The consultation closes on 5 January before final proposals go to Cabinet.
points: Council officers trained as enforcers, backed by new CCTV
Final proposals will go to Cabinet for a decision

stories.headline: County Hall finance chief warns of 'existential threat' as Essex budget gap could reach £476m by 2030
stories.summary: Essex County Council's cabinet member for finance, Bo Davis, says the gap between spending and income will keep widening without action, with social care driving most of the pressure, as a public budget consultation runs until 6 December.
body: Essex County Council faces a budget gap of nearly £170 million in 2027/28 if no further action is taken, rising to £280 million the year after, £384 million in 2029/30 and £476 million by 2030/31, according to figures reported by the Local Democracy Reporting Service. Cabinet member for finance Bo Davis, of Reform UK, described it as the biggest threat the council had faced in a long time, and the council is asking residents where money should go in a consultation on its 2027/28 budget.

About 70 per cent of next year's pressure is in social care, with extra spending expected of £45 million on adult social care, £64 million on children's care, £32 million on children's placements and £15 million on home-to-school transport. The council's 2026/27 net cost of services came to about £1,437 million, roughly £56 million more than budgeted. Council leader Peter Harris has argued that the government's funding settlement has not been fair to Essex taxpayers.

Mr Davis said it was too early to discuss council tax, currently £1,641.96 for a Band D home, and that no decisions had been made; reserves of around £600 million would be used only for transformation or bridging where absolutely necessary. He has contacted the Liberal Democrat, Conservative and independent group leaders seeking cross-party work on savings. The consultation closes on 6 December and the cabinet is due to consider budget proposals on 15 January 2027.
points: Gap of nearly £170m in 2027/28, rising to £476m by 2030/31 without action
Social care accounts for about 70% of next year's pressure
Band D council tax is £1,641.96; no decision on any change

stories.headline: Parish councils object as Saturday deadline nears for comments on data centre at Little Canfield's old Crumps Farm landfill
stories.summary: Little Canfield and Great Canfield parish councils have raised fears over contaminated land, water supply and the countryside as Essex County Council weighs the 10,240 sq m scheme near Dunmow.
body: The application to Essex County Council, as the waste planning authority, also covers cleaning up and restoring the old landfill, extra landfill infrastructure and a ground-mounted solar array on the southern part of the site, the Bishop's Stortford Independent reports.

Little Canfield and Great Canfield parish councils have raised concerns about building on contaminated land, local water supply and the countryside. The Environment Agency, a statutory consultee, is separately investigating claims of illegal waste dumping there. Public comments close on Saturday 14 November.
points: Essex County Council will decide the application
Public consultation closes on 14 November

stories.headline: Southend's fenced-off Three Shells Lagoon should be removed and the beach restored, council report says
stories.summary: Southend-on-Sea City Council says taking out the failed lagoon is its preferred long-term option, and the proposal goes to Cabinet on 16 November.
body: Returning the site to a natural beach came out on top after a technical assessment of several options, the report says. The Joint Administration has committed to resolving the long-running problems with the seafront scheme.

The council said the lagoon has already used a significant amount of public money and remains fenced off and unusable despite past investment. Cllr Matt Dent, Cabinet Member for Business, Culture, Music and Tourism, described it as no longer fit for purpose and said the council needed to "cut our losses". Your Southend reports that demolition would cost about £800,000, taking the total spent on the lagoon to around £2.84 million once its £1.95 million build and roughly £90,000 of attempted fixes are included.

The proposal will be considered by the council's Cabinet on Monday 16 November 2026. If it is approved, and planning permission, marine licences and final funding are secured, work could start in spring 2027 and take eight to ten weeks, with some of the rock possibly reused in the East Beach dune restoration at Shoeburyness.
points: Report recommends removing the lagoon structure and restoring a natural beach
Demolition would cost about £800,000, Your Southend reports
Work could start in spring 2027 if Cabinet agrees

stories.headline: Maldon MP and council leader urge Home Secretary to drop plan for asylum seekers to live in Tillingham
stories.summary: The Home Office has approved buying a property in the Dengie village for up to six people under its national dispersal scheme, Maldon District Council says.
points: Concerns also raised with Dame Priti Patel and the Chief Constable of Essex
No Home Office response has been reported
body: Council leader Simon Morgan has written to Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood arguing that remote Tillingham, with limited public transport and few services, is not a suitable place, and Maldon MP Sir John Whittingdale has asked her to reverse the decision, Maldon Nub News reports.
The council says the Home Office alone chooses properties. It has asked for more detail so it can offer support if the placement goes ahead.

stories.headline: c2c trains to call at Purfleet, Rainham and Dagenham Dock again from Wednesday after Barking derailment repairs
stories.summary: Passenger services through the stretch shut since a freight train came off the tracks near Barking on 23 October are due back on Wednesday 11 November, ending almost three weeks of rail replacement buses for Purfleet commuters.
body: c2c says passenger trains will resume calling at Dagenham Dock, Rainham and Purfleet from Wednesday 11 November, after the line near Barking was closed by the derailment of a GB Railfreight train on 23 October. The closure has left Purfleet and Rainham passengers relying on replacement buses to Grays and Upminster for nearly three weeks.

RailAdvent reports that engineers have repaired more than 1.2km of track, including rebuilding a damaged set of specially made points. Network Rail has confirmed the reopening, which also brings back London Overground trains between South Tottenham and Barking Riverside. Rob Mullen of GBR Anglia said he was pleased passenger services would return on Wednesday.

Until then, trains do not stop at the three stations and passengers are advised not to travel from them. Rail replacement buses run between Upminster and Grays via Rainham and Purfleet, and tickets are accepted on Greater Anglia and on TfL buses. Separately, London-bound trains are still not stopping at Limehouse while work continues there.
points: More than 1.2km of track and a set of points repaired
Replacement buses Upminster to Grays run until services resume
London-bound trains still not calling at Limehouse

stories.headline: Walk-in X-rays and new scans coming to St Margaret's diagnostic centre in Epping from mid-December
stories.summary: Blood tests move into the new community diagnostic centre at St Margaret's Hospital on 16 November, with X-ray, ultrasound and liver scans following on 14 December.
body: Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust says the Epping centre will have room for about 230 blood test patients a day once the service moves across from outpatients. The two walk-in X-ray rooms will be for patients referred by their GP.
A fourth ultrasound room and FibroScan liver checks also start on 14 December, adding about 350 patients a day. Chief executive Thom Lafferty called it an important step forward for diagnostic care.
points: Endoscopy appointments due in early 2027

stories.headline: Temporary housing for homeless families drives Basildon Council towards a £3.8m overspend this year
stories.summary: A half-year report warns reserves of £41.1m could be largely used up by 2029/30 if gaps keep being covered from savings, though it calls that a scenario rather than a forecast.
body: Basildon Council's general fund is forecast to finish 2026/27 £3.8m over budget, up £0.4m since June, according to a half-year report reported by Basildon Today. Housing accounts for £2.4m of the gap, £1.5m of it temporary accommodation, while the council housing account is £3.2m over.
Councillors on the finance scrutiny committee discuss the report on Monday 16 November before it goes to cabinet on 26 November.
points: Temporary accommodation forecast at £7.6m against a £6.1m budget
Council housing account £3.2m over, improved from £4.5m in June
Scrutiny committee meets on 16 November, cabinet on 26 November

stories.headline: Ambulance chief paramedic admits past misogyny as Essex councillors hear sexual safety sackings rose sixfold
stories.summary: Simon Chase told County Hall's health scrutiny committee there is no place for such behaviour, as campaigners warn some staff who quit mid-investigation may move to new employers.
body: The East of England Ambulance Service, which covers Essex, dismissed 25 staff over sexual safety cases in 2025/26, up from four the year before, according to figures from the trust's annual report reported by the Local Democracy Reporting Service. Reports more than doubled over the same period, and the trust says the rise reflects staff feeling more confident to speak up.

Chief paramedic Simon Chase told Essex County Council's health scrutiny committee that complaints had covered bullying, religion-related issues and sexual harassment, and acknowledged there had been examples of misogyny in the past. The number of staff who resigned while under investigation rose from five to 10, and campaign group Surviving in Scrubs says the true scale is likely higher.

The group warned that unless a worker is referred to the paramedics' regulator, there is no robust way for employers to share information, so some may move on to new jobs. The trust says it takes every allegation seriously and has brought in an independent body to review its complaints procedures; 40 cases were still open in March.
points: 156 cases have been logged since April 2024
Resignations during investigations rose from five to 10
An independent review of complaints handling is under way
stories.source: Greatest Hits Radio Essex (Local Democracy Reporting Service)

stories.headline: Thurrock's last chance to comment on plan for nearly 29,000 homes has now closed
stories.summary: The plan, which runs to 2044, will now go forward to an independent inspector, with West Horndon earmarked for about 10,000 of the new homes.
body: Thurrock Council's final round of comments on its draft Local Plan closed at midnight on Tuesday, Your Thurrock reports. The plan sets out room for at least 28,880 new homes up to 2044, with about 5,000 more across Lower Langdon and Corringham Park Farm, 4,787 at South Ockendon and 3,000 at Purfleet-on-Thames.
This stage only tests whether the plan is lawful and sound, not whether people back individual sites. The deadline had already been extended once after a site was left out of an environmental report.
points: Almost 3,000 homes are also proposed at Chadwell St Mary
Town centre renewal is planned for Grays, Purfleet-on-Thames and Lakeside

stories.headline: State Fayre claims a UK camping festival first with an all-female headline bill at Hylands Park
stories.summary: The Chicks, Kacey Musgraves and Shania Twain will top the country and Americana festival in Chelmsford from 18 to 20 June 2027.
body: State Fayre, the country, Americana and barbecue festival that launched at Hylands Park in Chelmsford this year, has named The Chicks and Kacey Musgraves as headliners for its second edition. They join Shania Twain, announced earlier this month, completing what organisers describe as the first all-female headline bill at a major UK camping festival.

The first wave of other acts includes Billy Strings, The Corrs, Brothers Osborne, Sam Barber and Bear's Den, with more to be added. Organisers Anna-Sophie Mertens and Alex Simmonds said the three headliners had each inspired change in their own way. The 2026 debut, headlined by Kings of Leon, Neil Young and The Lumineers, drew more than 50,000 people, the festival says.
Weekend and Saturday tickets are already on sale, a presale for Friday and Sunday day tickets is running, and general sale for those days opens at 9am on Friday 13 November.
points: Billy Strings and The Corrs are in the first wave of other acts
Friday and Sunday day tickets go on general sale at 9am on 13 November
More than 50,000 attended the first State Fayre, organisers say

stories.headline: Bus journeys starting in Thurrock to cost no more than £2 from Monday under festive fare cap
stories.summary: The Department for Transport is paying for the scheme, which arrives ahead of a planned national cap at the same level from January.
body: Thurrock Council has confirmed the Festive Fare Cap runs until 31 December and covers every single journey that starts in the borough.
Deputy leader Alan Benson, who holds the transport portfolio, said cheaper fares would help residents reach work, training, healthcare and local shops while living costs remain a worry.
points: Runs from 16 November to 31 December
The current national single fare cap is £3
The national change was announced by transport minister Lord Hendy in July

stories.headline: Thurrock Council launches review of its libraries and asks residents for their views
stories.summary: A borough-wide needs assessment will shape a new Library Strategy, with the council pointing to housing growth, transport changes and local government reorganisation.
body: Thurrock Council has begun a library needs assessment across the borough to gather evidence for a new Library Strategy, and is inviting residents to share their views through its consultation page. The announcement does not propose closures or changes to any named library or hub.
Cabinet member for heritage and culture George Monk said libraries support learning and community connections for all ages.
points: No closures or changes to specific buildings are named in the announcement
Monk wants to hear from people who have never visited a library
The council says the strategy will meet its statutory duties

stories.headline: Southend council says it cannot step in to reopen Leigh North Street school's shut swimming pool
stories.summary: A report for Monday's cabinet says the pool's future is a matter for the school, despite a petition signed by more than 2,500 people.
body: Leigh North Street Primary School closed its pool in July after the head teacher said it had become too costly to run. A report going to Southend-on-Sea City Council's cabinet on Monday 16 November concludes the council has no power to intervene, the BBC's local democracy reporter says.

Campaigners have raised more than £17,000 towards a £20,000 target and are looking at forming a charity or taking the pool into community ownership. Governors say they would consider a workable community-led plan, but none has yet been submitted.
points: Petition to the council gathered 2,547 signatures
Cabinet member Chris Webster called the school's decision disappointing
Save North Street Pool fundraising has passed £17,000

stories.headline: Some Tendring households miss bin collections as council cites technical problems
stories.summary: The Gazette reports that bins went unemptied in parts of the Tendring district because of what were described as technical issues.

stories.headline: Brentwood centre for rape and sexual assault survivors reopens after refit with new aftercare rooms
stories.summary: The Essex Sexual Assault Referral Centre, paid for by the county's police commissioner with Essex Police, stays in the county so survivors need not travel elsewhere.
body: The Essex Sexual Assault Referral Centre in Brentwood has reopened after a refurbishment that brought upgraded medical equipment, secure storage for forensic evidence, tighter security and new rooms for aftercare following an examination, Your Thurrock reports.

Medical, practical and emotional help is offered to adults and children whether or not they go to the police. Commissioner Roger Hirst welcomed the reopening, and the Victims Commissioning Fund will help with future running costs.
points: Changes include better access for people with sight, hearing or mobility needs

stories.headline: GMB opens strike ballot at G4S Cash in Harlow, raising prospect of action before Christmas
stories.summary: Staff at the cash handling site are under a pay freeze, the union says, and voting runs until midday on 25 November.
body: GMB members at G4S Cash in Harlow have begun voting on industrial action after a two-year pay claim lodged in September made no satisfactory progress, Your Harlow reports. The union wants an urgent pay meeting, a deal for 2026 and a firm offer for 2027, and says action could follow in the run-up to Christmas if the company does not return to talks.
points: No statement from G4S was reported

stories.headline: Festoon lights back on Southend Pier for the first time in over 20 years, with switch-on set for Saturday
stories.summary: More than a mile of lights will run the length of the pier, launching an evening of festive events across the city on 14 November.
body: Southend Pier's festoon lighting is returning for the first time in more than two decades, Southend-on-Sea City Council has announced. More than a mile of the lights will stretch along the world's longest pleasure pier, and new colourful neon lighting and light-up benches have been added at the On the Decks area at the Pier Head.

The official pier switch-on is at 5pm on Saturday 14 November, with music, food and drinks at the Royal Pavilion afterwards. Council leader Daniel Cowan said the council had promised to bring the lights back and had done so, while cabinet member Matt Dent called it a special occasion for the city.

The same evening the main city centre Christmas lights are switched on at Victoria Circus at 6pm, followed by the season's last seafront fireworks at 7.30pm. Southend City BID's Christmas in the City runs on the High Street during the day, with an artisan market, live music and family activities.
points: Pier open 10.15am to 8pm on the day
Walking admission £3.10 for adults, £2.10 for children and concessions

stories.summary: October brought 2.79 million travellers through the Uttlesford airport, up 4.2% on the same month last year.
body: London Stansted had its busiest day on record on Sunday 25 October, the Bishop's Stortford Independent reports, as school half-term getaways and overseas visitors pushed numbers up. Managing director Gareth Powell called October another landmark month for the airport, which handles nearly 31 million passengers a year and has permission to grow to 51 million.
points: More than 101,000 people flew to or from Istanbul in October
Dublin and Edinburgh were the next busiest destinations
Spain was the most popular country, ahead of Italy and Turkey

stories.summary: Chelmsford city centre's Christmas lights switch-on is set for a Sunday, rounding off a full day of festive entertainment, Chelmsford City News reports.

stories.headline: Burnham-on-Crouch signs friendship pact with Carpathian town of Yaremche
stories.summary: Burnham-on-Crouch Town Council has become the first in Essex to twin with a Ukrainian community, linking the River Crouch town with Yaremche in the Ivano-Frankivsk region.
body: Burnham-on-Crouch Town Council held a twinning ceremony with Yaremche, a town on the River Prut in Ukraine's Carpathian Mountains, at 10am on Thursday 12 November 2026, the Lviv Herald reports. The event in the council chambers was set to include a memorandum of friendship and cooperation and an exchange of civic gifts.
The link was built by Councillor Stephen Stratton through talks with Yaremche's mayor, Andriy Myronyak. Burnham has been twinned with L'Aiguillon-sur-Mer in France since 1980.
points: Mayor Councillor Douglas Bown opened the ceremony
Yaremche relied on tourism before Russia's full-scale invasion and has housed displaced people

stories.headline: Tilbury youth zone on track for 2027 as charity warns of isolated generation
stories.summary: Building work continues on the OnSide Youth Zone in Tilbury, which will offer climbing, music production, fitness and affordable hot meals for Thurrock's young people.
body: Construction is continuing on the OnSide Youth Zone in Tilbury, which is due to open in 2027, Thurrock Nub News reported on Thursday 12 November 2026. Bethanie Cundy, chief executive of OnSide Youth Zone Thames Gateway, said the charity's Generation Isolation findings showed why the centre matters for Thurrock.
OnSide says only 11% of young people in the South East attend youth clubs, and is asking local businesses to back the project.
points: 34.5% of Thurrock children aged 5 to 16 are physically active, against 47.8% nationally
OnSide wants more recognition and funding for youth workers

stories.headline: Interactive artwork about living with MS and Parkinson's goes on show at Tilbury library
stories.summary: Thurrock dance charity CoDa has brought its Beyond the Darkness installation to Tilbury Library and Hub until Monday 7 December.
body: CoDa Dance Company, a Thurrock dance charity, has opened its award-winning interactive installation Beyond the Darkness at Tilbury Library and Hub, Thurrock Nub News reported on Thursday 12 November 2026. It pairs a sensor screen that gets visitors moving with short dance films about life with multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's and acquired brain injury, made with neuro-disabled consultants.
Artistic director Nikki Watson founded the charity in 2013. The work was shown earlier at the Thameside in Grays.
points: Entry is free and the space is fully accessible to wheelchair users
CoDa also runs weekly Dance for Neurology sessions in hospitals

stories.headline: Batteries thrown out with household rubbish blamed for Colchester bin lorry fire
stories.summary: A bin lorry caught fire in Colchester, with the blaze put down to batteries that had been thrown away in household waste.

stories.headline: Chelmsford MP says Broomfield Hospital trust's recovery plan is moving too slowly
stories.summary: Marie Goldman wants clearer reporting on how the intensive NHS programme for Mid and South Essex will be judged, while the trust says waiting lists are already falling.
body: Liberal Democrat MP for Chelmsford Marie Goldman has criticised the pace of the intensive recovery programme for Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust, which runs Broomfield Hospital, Chelmsford City Hub reported on Wednesday 11 November 2026. The programme began in September 2026, about six months after it was announced in March.
The trust says the programme is already shortening waiting lists and speeding up discharges, and the Department of Health and Social Care says early signs of progress are emerging.
points: 50.4% of the trust's planned-care patients were within 18 weeks, against a national median of 65.2%
She raised the issue in a Westminster Hall debate on 14 October

stories.headline: Southend Hospital becomes first in Essex to win Sophie's Legacy award for looking after children's families
stories.summary: Southend Hospital's Neptune children's ward now provides meals for parents staying with their child and play specialists seven days a week.
body: Only five other hospitals in the country hold the accreditation, Chelmsford City Hub reports. Sophie's Legacy was set up by Charlotte Fairall in memory of her daughter Sophie, who died of a rare childhood cancer, and hospitals must meet at least three of its five aims for families. The ward worked with caterer Medirest on the changes, which include a children's menu. Amy Taylor, associate director of nursing for paediatrics, said caring for a child also means caring for their family.
points: Charity also gave sensory toys and essentials packs for parents
Changes include a new children's menu

stories.headline: Writtle restaurant Pakwaan is the only Essex name in national Indian food guide's top 100
stories.summary: Pakwaan Indian Punjabi Cuisine on Bridge Street, Writtle, near Chelmsford, made the British Indian Good Food Guide's 2026 selection.
body: The guide announced its 2026 selection on Tuesday 10 November and placed Pakwaan in its South Coast, East and Home Counties section, Chelmsford City Hub reports. The guide says the list is an editorial choice rather than a ranked league table.
points: Guide's numbering is not a national ranking

stories.headline: Forecasters tip Harlow Conservatives to tighten grip on council next May, with Labour down to six seats
stories.summary: A seat-by-seat model of next year's Harlow District Council elections gives Reform UK nothing and leaves the Conservatives with a bigger majority.
body: Election Maps UK's projection for May 2027 puts the Conservatives on 27 of Harlow District Council's 33 seats, up from 22, Your Harlow reported on 11 November. The Tories won all eleven wards in May 2026, and Labour currently holds 10 seats and Reform UK one.
The model suggests Reform could lose its Mark Hall seat. Your Harlow says it will publish its own forecast in April.
points: Labour seats in Bush Fair, Little Parndon, Netteswell and Passmores in question
Council leader is Conservative Dan Swords

councilwatch.headline: Developer appeals over lack of decision on 910 green belt homes at Billericay's Foots Farm
councilwatch.summary: Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee was asked to say how it would have decided the Great Burstead scheme, after an appeal was lodged because no decision had been made. Officers backed the plan, which offers more than £20 million in contributions.
body: Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee considered an outline application for up to 910 homes on land at Foots Farm, Southend Road, Great Burstead, near Billericay, on Tuesday 3 November 2026. Because the applicant had already lodged an appeal on the grounds of non-determination, councillors were asked to indicate the decision they would have made had the application stayed with the council. Officers recommended that outline planning permission would have been granted.

The report says the 56.89 hectare site is farmland in the Metropolitan Green Belt and that the scheme counts as inappropriate development, but officers concluded its benefits significantly outweigh the harm. Half the homes would be affordable, with eight Gypsy and Traveller pitches, a community hub and 3.44 hectares safeguarded for a nursery and three-form entry primary school. The Section 106 package of more than £20 million covers education, healthcare, bus services, play and sports, and employment and skills, and the site forms part of the South East Billericay allocation in the emerging Basildon Local Plan.

Three residents and the chair of the parish council spoke against the plan, citing the loss of Green Belt and farmland, traffic on Coxes Farm Road and Bell Hill, and pressure on schools, GP services, water supply and drainage. Councillors also complained that a technical briefing had been arranged without consulting the committee's chair and vice-chair and without Essex County Council Highways, and it was agreed to seek Highways representation at future meetings. The application will now be settled through the appeal.
points: Up to 910 homes, 50% affordable, on 56.89 hectares of Green Belt

body: Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee agreed on Tuesday 3 November 2026 the formal reason for refusing outline permission for up to 175 homes on land west of Tye Common Road, Little Burstead, near Billericay. Councillors had resolved to refuse the scheme at their meeting on Wednesday 7 October 2026, and the wording was brought back for agreement. The agreed reason says the site makes a strong contribution to the Green Belt's purpose of checking urban sprawl, so it does not count as grey belt, and the homes would cause substantial harm to the openness of the Green Belt. The committee was not satisfied that the benefits clearly outweighed that harm. body: Tendring District Council's Planning Policy and Local Plan Committee will meet on Tuesday 17 November 2026 to hear the results of the final public consultation on the district's new Local Plan, held in September and October 2026. Councillors are asked to recommend to Full Council that the plan be submitted to the Secretary of State for independent examination by a planning inspector. Officers say they remain of the view that the plan is legally compliant and sound.

The report says government targets require Tendring to plan for 1,069 homes a year, nearly double the figure in its previous plan. The council aims to submit before the end of 2026, even though the government has extended the cut-off to the end of March 2027, to avoid restarting under a new system. Fewer people responded than at the previous stage, when 628 respondents made about 2,200 comments, mainly because the council dropped two of the most opposed sites, at Brightlingsea and Walton.

The most opposed remaining site is the planned 450 homes north of Thorpe Road, Kirby Cross, with about 45 objections, and the report notes Taylor Wimpey has been consulting on up to 500 homes there, with an application possible in December. A 2,600-name petition, around 500 of them from the Manningtree, Lawford and Mistley area, backed keeping Lawford Tye as protected open space, and 12 of Tendring's 27 town and parish councils responded. The final decision to submit rests with Full Council, and the inspector may require changes before the plan can be adopted.

councilwatch.headline: Maldon scraps area planning committees and councillor call-in as new national rules take effect
councilwatch.summary: Maldon District Council now has one 13-member Planning Committee, with most applications decided by officers under a new national scheme of delegation.
body: Maldon District Council agreed on Thursday 22 October 2026 to set up a single Planning Committee of 13 members from Saturday 31 October 2026. It abolished the North Western, Central and South Eastern Area Planning Committees and the District Planning Committee on the same date. Councillors were told the change was required by the Town and Country Planning (Discharge of Local Planning Authority Functions) (England) Regulations 2026, which came into force on 31 October.

Under the new National Scheme of Delegation, routine and minor applications go to officers, and larger or more sensitive ones are also delegated unless they pass a threshold known as the Gateway Test. There is no longer a process for councillors to call in applications. Councillor W Stamp said she did not consider the changes democratic and asked for her vote against to be recorded.

The new committee is due to meet every three weeks at 7pm, mostly on Wednesdays, with meetings cancelled when there is no business. A separate report to the same meeting proposed a revised public speaking protocol that would let ward councillors who do not sit on the committee speak on applications in their wards, raise speaking time from two to three minutes, and allow electronic voting.
points: One 13-member Planning Committee from 31 October 2026
Four previous planning committees abolished
No councillor call-in under the national scheme
Meetings every three weeks at 7pm when there is business

councilwatch.summary: Maldon District Council councillors have asked for a full breakdown, including officer time, of spending on the Mid Essex council plan before the government paused the Essex shake-up.
body: Maldon District Council received a report from its Chief Executive on Thursday 22 October 2026 setting out what it spent preparing for a Mid Essex unitary council before the government paused local government reorganisation. Councillors agreed to ask for a full breakdown of the costs, including officer time, and details of how the Mid Essex Director was appointed.

The report says the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government withdrew the five-unitary model for Essex on 7 September 2026 and paused reorganisation for review. Costs between the choice of that model and the pause are estimated at £78,000, with Maldon expected to pay a third, about £26,000, for IT, a councillor engagement event, staff support and specialist project management. No posts were recruited specifically for the work, and earlier Freedom of Information requests about the costs were refused because the figures were due to be published.

The final figure is due to be confirmed by the Mid Essex Programme Board in November, and the council is still waiting to hear whether there are Essex-wide costs to share. Councillors were also told that Essex County Council has consented to a Greater Essex mayoral strategic authority with Southend-on-Sea City Council and Thurrock Council, though all three must agree, and that the first mayoral election is now planned for May 2028.

councilwatch.headline: Government direction pushes Southend's draft local plan towards a six-week public consultation
councilwatch.summary: The new plan would set the rules for where homes go and how the council handles applications for shared houses, affordable housing and hot food takeaways.
body: Southend-on-Sea City Council's cabinet held an extraordinary meeting on 5 November 2026 to consider the final draft of the city's new Local Plan. A report from the Executive Director (Environment and Place) sought agreement to comply with a government direction by publishing the Regulation 19 Proposed Submission version of the plan for a consultation lasting at least six weeks. At this stage residents and others can comment on whether the plan is sound and legally compliant.

The minutes say national policy requires every council to keep an up-to-date local plan, which allocates sites for development and sets the policies used to decide planning applications. Councillors were told the existing Development Plan is out of date and no longer reflects major social, environmental and economic changes. The reasons recorded for the decision warn that without a plan development would not stop, but would be more likely to come forward in an uncoordinated and speculative way, with less supporting infrastructure and fewer protections for existing residents.

The papers say new criteria-based policies would give the council a more robust, evidenced approach to applications including Houses in Multiple Occupation, affordable housing and hot food takeaways. The meeting papers include the draft plan, a policies map, a report on the earlier Regulation 18 consultation, a sustainability appraisal and an updated Local Development Scheme setting out the timetable. Three questions from councillors were answered at the meeting and published with the minutes.

body: Southend-on-Sea City Council's external auditor, KPMG, reported on its audit of the council's accounts for the year ended 31 March 2026 at the Audit and Governance Committee on 19 October 2026. body: Southend-on-Sea City Council's Audit and Governance Committee received an update on 19 October 2026 on the council's progress in responding to a judgement by the Regulator of Social Housing. The Head of Housing told the committee that monthly meetings with the regulator were continuing and that significant progress had been made on the council's Provider Improvement Plan. The council has reached 100% coverage of electrical safety checks in communal areas and 99% in homes, and the minutes say the regulator now regards electrical safety as business as usual. Repairs remain an area of focus, and a targeted improvement plan has been agreed with the council's repairs contractor to cut work in progress and bring performance up to industry norms by Christmas 2026.

Councillors were told the Housing Ombudsman's investigation has concluded, with the council due to submit a learning statement as the final stage. Officers said this was the first inspection under the new consumer regulation framework and that the council knew of areas needing improvement before the inspections took place. The committee asked for a further update on repairs performance.

body: Thurrock Council's Children's Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee was told on 22 October 2026 that 75% of initial health assessments for children entering care are now completed within the statutory 20-day timescale. The figure compares with 36% previously, according to the minutes of the meeting.

Officers put the improvement down to closer joint working with Children's Services, more paediatric capacity and better oversight. They said late assessments were mainly caused by changes of placement, hospital admissions, missed appointments and occasional staff absence, and that only one delayed assessment in the reporting period was down to a lack of capacity.

The service is moving to a model led by specialist nurses working with paediatricians, and officers said a formal review in December 2026 will look at the views of children and families, the quality of assessments and timeliness. Councillors questioned whether enough paediatric capacity would remain, and officers said the aim was to use existing paediatric resources more effectively. The committee noted the update.

councilwatch.summary: A motion to full council called for the district's maximum fixed penalty for fly-tipping to rise fivefold now that the law allows it.
body: A motion put to Epping Forest District Council's full council meeting on 22 October 2026 asked councillors to support, in principle, raising the council's maximum fixed penalty notice for fly-tipping from £1,000 to £5,000. It was proposed by Councillor K Rizvi and seconded by Councillor C McCann. The published papers do not yet record the outcome.

The motion says the council can currently issue fines of up to £1,000 for fly-tipping, but recent changes to the law now allow councils to set a maximum of £5,000. It argues that people who deliberately dump waste should face a penalty reflecting the damage to the environment and the costs borne by residents.

If backed, the motion asks the Cabinet Member for Environment and Regulatory Services to work with the council's environmental enforcement team to bring in the higher fine as soon as practicable, subject to legal and constitutional requirements. It also calls for clear public communication and continued enforcement, and encourages residents to keep reporting fly-tipping with photographs, CCTV or dashcam footage where they have it.

The report from the Portfolio Holder for Housing and Planning recommends adoption, including revised conservation area boundaries where applicable.

The report says both documents were shaped by public consultations held between 2022 and 2026, and that responses led to changes, including to some boundaries. They are the last two in a programme to review all 20 of the district's conservation areas, a priority of the Tendring Heritage Strategy, which includes five areas on Historic England's Heritage at Risk Register.

councilwatch.headline: Tendring budgets for life beyond 2028 as the government pauses the council shake-up
councilwatch.summary: With Whitehall reviewing its plan to replace Essex's councils, Tendring's cabinet has agreed to plan four years ahead, and backed money for toilets, playgrounds and housing staff.
body: Tendring District Council's cabinet has agreed to refresh the council's financial forecast over four years, to allow for the possibility that the council still exists after April 2028. That date had been the proposed start for a new unitary council under the government's original timetable for Greater Essex, but on 7 September 2026 the government announced it would pause and review its local government reorganisation programme.

The report to cabinet on 23 October said the pause had brought a significant level of uncertainty for the councils affected, though Tendring's two-year financial plan still left it in a positive position. If reorganisation goes ahead, even later than planned, the forecast can be switched back to the council's earlier approach of preparing for a handover to the new authority.

Cabinet also approved changes to this year's budget, including £540,000 for housing capacity and restructuring, £100,000 to invest in public toilets and £400,000 for project delivery capacity, and accepted £270,000 from the government's Playground Fund. The report said the general fund was £3.669m underspent against its profiled budget at the end of July, largely because of the timing of spending.
